request.title: Add priorities to tasks
request.body: Every task has a priority: low, normal or high. It is normal unless the user says otherwise. The add command accepts --priority followed by a level after the title, for example add Pay rent --priority high. An unknown level is an error and nothing is added. The list command shows high priority tasks first, then normal, then low, keeping the order they were added in within each level. A task whose priority is not normal shows it in brackets after the title, for example "[ ] 2 Pay rent (high)". Everything that works today must keep working, and the existing tests must still pass. Plain ES modules, no dependencies.

artifact.title: Task Priority System
artifact.problem: Tasks currently lack a way to indicate importance, making it difficult for users to organize and prioritize their work within the task list.
goals: Allow users to assign a priority level (low, normal, high) to tasks during creation.
Ensure tasks are sorted by priority in the list view.
Visually indicate non-normal priority levels in the task list.
nonGoals: Updating the priority of an existing task.
Adding new priority levels beyond low, normal, and high.
Filtering the list to show only specific priorities.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: When a task is added without the --priority flag, the task is assigned a priority of 'normal'.
When a task is added using 'add [title] --priority high', the task is saved with high priority.
When a task is added using 'add [title] --priority normal', the task is saved with normal priority.
When a task is added using 'add [title] --priority low', the task is saved with low priority.
When a task is added with an unsupported priority level (e.g., 'add [title] --priority urgent'), the system returns an error and no task is added to the store.
When the list command is executed, tasks are displayed in the order of High, then Normal, then Low.
When multiple tasks have the same priority level, they are displayed in the order they were originally added.
In the list view, tasks with 'high' or 'low' priority display the priority level in brackets after the title (e.g., '[ ] 1 Task Name (high)').
In the list view, tasks with 'normal' priority do not display any priority label after the title.

artifact.approach: Extend the task data model to include a priority field and implement a custom sort order in the list view. The CLI will be updated to parse the --priority flag and validate it against a set of allowed values (low, normal, high). The formatting logic will be updated to conditionally append the priority label.

components.name: CLI Handler
components.responsibility: Parse command line arguments for the 'add' command, specifically extracting and validating the --priority flag.

components.name: Task Store
components.responsibility: Persist tasks with their associated priority and retrieve tasks sorted by priority level and then by insertion order.

components.name: Output Formatter
components.responsibility: Format the task string for display, appending the priority label only for non-normal levels.

interfaces.contract: Updates to the 'add' command logic to handle the '--priority [value]' argument. If absent, defaults to 'normal'. If invalid, throws an error preventing store insertion.

saveTask(task, priority): saves task with priority string. 
getTasks(): returns an array of tasks sorted by priority (High > Normal > Low), then by original sequence.
formatTask(task): returns a string. If task.priority is 'high' or 'low', appends ' (priority)' to the title. If 'normal', appends nothing.

decisions.title: Priority Weighting
decisions.decision: Use a numeric mapping (high: 0, normal: 1, low: 2) internally for sorting.
decisions.rationale: Allows for a simple stable sort that meets AC-6 and AC-7 without complex conditional logic in the sort comparator.

decisions.title: Validation Location
decisions.decision: Perform priority validation in the CLI layer before calling the store.
decisions.rationale: Prevents invalid data from ever reaching the persistence layer, satisfying AC-5.

decisions.title: Default Value
decisions.decision: Implicitly assign 'normal' if the flag is missing.
decisions.rationale: Satisfies AC-1 and ensures the store always has a consistent schema for sorting.

risks: Adding a priority field to existing saved tasks in the store may lead to undefined values if the store is not migrated or handled with defaults during retrieval.

screens.name: Task List View
screens.purpose: Display all saved tasks sorted by priority (High > Normal > Low) and then by insertion order, with visual priority indicators for non-normal tasks.
states: Empty: Display a message indicating no tasks have been added yet.
Loading: Display a loading indicator while tasks are being retrieved from the store.
Populated: Display the list of tasks formatted according to priority rules (e.g., '1 Task Name (high)').
Error: Display an error message if the task store cannot be accessed.

screens.name: Task Creation Interface
screens.purpose: Allow users to input a task title and optionally specify a priority level (low, normal, high).
states: Submitting: Processing the 'add' command and saving to the store.
Success: Confirmation that the task was added successfully.
Invalid Priority Error: Display an error message when an unsupported priority level is provided (e.g., 'urgent'), preventing task creation.

components: Task Item: A row element showing the checkbox, index, title, and conditional priority label.
Priority Selector: A mechanism (CLI flag or UI dropdown) to choose between low, normal, and high.
Error Notification: A visual alert for invalid priority inputs or system failures.
accessibility: Ensure high color contrast for priority labels to make them distinguishable from the task title.
Use ARIA labels or screen-reader friendly text for the priority indicators (e.g., '[ ] 1 Task Name, priority high').
Provide clear focus management when error messages appear after an invalid priority input.
Ensure the task list is navigable via keyboard in the sorted order.

tasks.title: Update Task Store for Priority Persistence and Sorting
tasks.description: Modify the store to save tasks with a priority field and implement a retrieval method that sorts tasks by priority (High > Normal > Low) and then by their original insertion order using a numeric weighting system.

tasks.title: Implement Priority-Aware Task Formatting
tasks.description: Update the output formatter to append the priority level in brackets (e.g., '(high)') to the task title if the priority is 'high' or 'low'. If the priority is 'normal', no label should be appended.

tasks.title: Implement Priority Parsing and Validation in CLI
tasks.description: Update the CLI handler to parse the '--priority' flag for the 'add' command. Implement validation to only allow 'low', 'normal', and 'high'. Ensure 'normal' is assigned if the flag is missing, and return an error if an unsupported value is provided.

artifact.summary: Update formatTask to append priority label for high and low priorities.
Update the task store to support priority persistence and custom sorting (High > Normal > Low), while maintaining insertion order for tasks of the same priority.

findings.comment: The sort implementation fails AC-7. Array.prototype.sort() is not guaranteed to be stable in all environments (though it is in modern V8), but more importantly, by only comparing weights (weightA - weightB), the relative order of tasks with the same priority is not explicitly preserved. To ensure a stable sort by original sequence, the comparator must fall back to comparing task IDs (or indices) when weights are equal. Change the sort return to: 'return weightA - weightB || a.id - b.id;'.

reasons: [blocker] src/store.js: The sort implementation fails AC-7. Array.prototype.sort() is not guaranteed to be stable in all environments (though it is in modern V8), but more importantly, by only comparing weights (weightA - weightB), the relative order of tasks with the same priority is not explicitly preserved. To ensure a stable sort by original sequence, the comparator must fall back to comparing task IDs (or indices) when weights are equal. Change the sort return to: 'return weightA - weightB || a.id - b.id;'.

artifact.summary: Update the sort logic in src/store.js to ensure stable sorting by falling back to task IDs when priorities are equal, satisfying AC-7.
Update CLI handler to parse and validate the --priority flag for the 'add' command, defaulting to 'normal' and throwing an error for unsupported values.

AC-4: add task with low priority

AC-7: tasks of same priority maintain insertion order
AC-9: normal priority does not display label
